# Vendored tree-sitter grammars

sloplint parses with pinned grammar trees under `vendor/`. Each directory is
an upstream tree at a pinned commit plus a small patch series, with `src/`
regenerated so that valid real-world source stops reporting
`meta/parse-error`. The pins live in `vendor/grammars.toml`: one table per
vendored directory plus the crates.io dependency `tree-sitter-r`. The
manifest describes what is vendored today and never changes grammar content
by itself.

## Pinning policy

Prefer, in this order:

1. A published crate used unpatched, pinned exactly (version plus the crate
   `.cargo_vcs_info.json` commit). None of the vendored directories
   currently qualifies; `tree-sitter-r` is the only grammar consumed this
   way (workspace dependency, no vendor directory).
2. A vendored pristine upstream tree at a pinned commit. Today:
   `tree-sitter-quint` (grammar files verbatim) and `tree-sitter-racket`
   (no patch file; files byte-identical to the tag).
3. A vendored upstream tree plus a small, documented patch series that
   follows upstream. Every patch states its upstream PR or issue, or why
   there is none. `patch_status` in the manifest is `upstream-pending` with
   a `patch_upstream` URL when an upstream fix exists, else `local` with the
   reason in `notes`.
4. No self-authored grammars, except `tree-sitter-logos`, which is our own
   Go dialect and has no upstream.

Reuse or cherry-pick existing grammars; do not author grammars ourselves.

## Layout

Every vendored crate carries `sloplint-grammar.patch` (empty or absent only
where the manifest says `patch_status = "none"`) and `SLOPLINT.md`, which
records its upstream tag and remaining failures. `tree-sitter-php`,
`tree-sitter-typescript`, and `tree-sitter-ocaml` keep their upstream nested
layouts.

| Entry | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `grammar.js` | the grammar definition, carrying the patch |
| `src/` | regenerated by `tree-sitter generate` with the CLI version named in `grammars.toml` (`generator`) and `SLOPLINT.md`; `parser.c` and `src/tree_sitter/*.h` must come from the same CLI version |
| `sloplint-grammar.patch` | the diff of `grammar.js` (and touched scanner or corpus files) versus the pinned base |
| `test/corpus/` | the upstream corpus, vendored so `tree-sitter test` runs in place |
| `test/corpus/sloplint_*.txt` | new corpus cases for each fixed shape |
| `SLOPLINT.md` | provenance, regeneration command, what is fixed, what still fails |

ABI note: the vendored `src/parser.c` files carry `LANGUAGE_VERSION` 14
for `tree-sitter-c`, `tree-sitter-odin`, and `tree-sitter-tlaplus`
(generated with CLI 0.24.7), and 15 for everything else (generated with
CLI 0.27.x, except logos with 0.27.2 and quint with upstream 0.27.0).
`tree-sitter-cpp` and `tree-sitter-lean` commit `src/parser.c.gz` instead
of `src/parser.c`. The runtime (tree-sitter 0.27.2) loads ABI 13 through
15, so all vendored parsers load. The host CLI at
`/home/alpha/.cargo/bin/tree-sitter` is 0.24.7 and cannot read ABI 15
trees; use a 0.27.x CLI for those (the audit lanes keep one in scratch).

The workspace excludes `vendor/` (root `Cargo.toml`, `exclude = ["vendor"]`)
and each crate is referenced by a `path` dependency in
`[workspace.dependencies]`, so nothing here is re-published or rebuilt as
workspace code.

## Regenerating

In a grammar directory, after editing `grammar.js`:

```
tree-sitter generate
tree-sitter test
```

Use the CLI version from `grammars.toml` (`generator`) for that grammar.
Node is the JS runtime; `--js-runtime native` gives byte-identical
`parser.c`. Give every CLI run a private `TREE_SITTER_LIBDIR` and an
isolated `XDG_CACHE_HOME`: `tree-sitter parse` and `generate` in one
grammar directory otherwise reuse another grammar's cached parser of the
same name. Keep `sloplint-grammar.patch` in sync: it must hold exactly the
difference from the pinned base, and `SLOPLINT.md` must describe the change
and the regeneration provenance. Nested layouts need one `generate` per
grammar directory (`php/` and `php_only/`; `typescript/` and `tsx/`;
`grammars/ocaml`, `grammars/interface`, `grammars/type`).

### Baseline exception: tree-sitter-logos

`tree-sitter-logos` has no published crate, so its patch baseline is the
patched in-repo `tree-sitter-go` grammar instead.
`vendor/tree-sitter-logos/SLOPLINT.md` records that base and the reproduce
command; its `sloplint-grammar.patch` must hold exactly the difference from
that base.

## Checking the manifest

`bash scripts/grammars.sh check` validates `vendor/grammars.toml` offline:
directory coverage both ways, 40-hex commits (or `UNRESOLVED` only for
`tree-sitter-logos`), patch files present when `patch_status` is not
`none`, and Cargo name and version matches. It uses the host `python3`
(`tomllib` from the standard library); that is why the check is shell
rather than a Rust test, which would need a workspace build for the same
answer. CI runs this check in the `grammar-manifest` job. There is no
`justfile` in this repo; run the script directly.

`bash scripts/grammars.sh verify <name>` reproduces one tree from its
pinned upstream commit (shallow fetch, apply patch, generate with the
pinned CLI, diff `grammar.js` and `src/`). It needs network access and the
matching CLI version, so it is a manual or scheduled candidate, not a
required CI step. `bash scripts/grammars.sh bump <name> <commit>` prints
the follow-upstream steps without changing anything (unless `--write`,
which only updates the manifest commit field and still leaves re-vendoring
to the operator).

## Bumping a pin

1. `bash scripts/grammars.sh bump <name> <commit>` shows the fetch, diff,
   re-apply, regenerate, and manifest update steps.
2. Re-vendor from the new commit, re-apply the patch series, regenerate
   with the pinned CLI, run `tree-sitter test` and the
   `grammar_gaps` suite.
3. Update `grammars.toml` (`commit`, `tag`, `generator`) and the
   `SLOPLINT.md` provenance in the same commit as the re-vendor.

## Cherry-picked upstream commits

Keep upstream authorship: cherry-pick the upstream commit itself, do not
rewrite it as our own change. Record the upstream commit hash in the patch
header and in the manifest `notes` or `patch_upstream`, so the patch stays
easy to follow upstream and to drop once the fix releases.

## Why no cargo git dependencies

`deny.toml` sets `[sources] unknown-git = "deny"`, so only the crates.io
registry is allowed; cargo git dependencies are rejected by `cargo deny
check`. Vendoring keeps every grammar tree reviewable in the checkout and
keeps the build offline. Allowing git dependencies would need an owner
decision: relax the `unknown-git` rule, pin exact revs, and re-prove the
offline build.

## Regression tests

`crates/sloplint-syntax/tests/grammar_gaps/<language>.rs` pins every fixed
shape through `analyze`; each module records which cases fail against the
published grammar, so a re-vendor that drops a patch fails the suite.
